notes: Cognitive Science is currently taught in English, but AU anticipates a switch to Danish for autumn 2027. If implemented, Danish A and English B would be required. Check the programme page after 1 December 2026 before relying on an English-only pathway.
A, B and C are Danish subject levels, not grades. AU repeats this on each programme page: "B-level is the Danish subject level, not the grade."

AU publishes a quota 1 qualifying-examination GPA floor of 6.0 on the Danish 7-point scale for all six currently English-taught campus paths. For Economics and Business Administration in Herning, the Danish programme page states the floor while the English page omits it. Below the floor, applicants must use quota 2; this is not a universal IB minimum or a quota 2 floor. Cognitive Science's 2027 teaching language remains unconfirmed.
Computer Science, Data Science and IT Product Development add a second floor: a minimum GPA of 6.0 in Mathematics A specifically, on top of the overall 6.0.
The 6.0 floor is not the cut-off. The cut-off is what the last admitted applicant actually scored, and in 2026 that was 11.4 for Computer Science and 11.2 for Data Science.

AU tells "Danish applicants" (on its Data Science page, "applicants with Danish A") to treat the English-taught Computer Science, Data Science and IT Product Development degrees as the harder route and to apply to the Danish-taught equivalents (Datalogi, Datavidenskab, It-produktudvikling) as well. For Data Science AU says outright that the English version "is intended for international students". The two versions lead to the same English-taught master's.

The standby cut-off is published next to the quota 1 cut-off and is usually lower — dramatically so for IT Product Development in 2026 (10.1 in quota 1, 6.9 for standby). You have to tick standby when you apply, and the standby application deadline is 5 July.

Herning is not Aarhus. AU Herning is a small campus roughly an hour west of Aarhus in a town of about 50,000, running a few business, engineering and technology programmes. Its Economics and Business Administration degree is academically similar to the Aarhus one but had a 2026 cut-off of 6.9 against 9.2.

Paying applicants cannot apply in the year they earn the IB: their final diploma and transcripts are due 15 March at noon. Non-EU/EEA/Swiss applicants must establish their actual tuition/residence exemption status; a Danish address alone is not a published tuition exemption.

For applications after 1 November 2026, the EUR 150 application fee is non-refundable even on enrolment, and the whole first year of tuition is paid before the first semester. The published tuition schedule is still 2026/27; 2027/28 rates are not yet published.

AU’s Course Results page still mentions GSK, while the national recognition authority distinguishes qualification supplementation through HF-enkeltfag from GSK subject-level supplementation. Follow the national qualification rule and confirm the individual route with AU.

The English first-year offerings listed here are in Aarhus and Herning. AU also has Emdrup (Copenhagen), Viborg/Foulum, Roskilde and Flakkebjerg locations; these are not additional campuses for the listed English degrees.

officialWording.text: International Baccalaureate (IB) med IB-Course Result på mindst 18 point sidestilles med en gymnasial eksamen, hvis ansøgeren har opnået mindst karakteren 3 i hvert af de 6 fag, der indgår i IB-forløbet. Endvidere skal ansøgeren have gennemført enkeltfag på gymnasialt niveau svarende til overbygning, jf. reglerne om overbygning i højere forberedelseseksamen (hf-eksamen) i lov om gymnasiale uddannelser.

requirements.alternativeRoute: It does not close this one to you. The Danish Agency treats DP Course Results of at least 18 points, with at least grade 3 in all six subjects and at least three of them at HL, as equivalent to a qualifying examination for a Danish university bachelor once you have added two successive raises in the level of upper-secondary subjects, at least one of them to A level, taken as hf-enkeltfag or as a self-study candidate. If you already hold an A-level subject other than Danish, two raises to B level are enough. Retaking to be awarded the full IB Diploma is the other published route.
requirements.note: AU’s Course Results page still mentions GSK, but national guidance distinguishes qualification supplementation through HF-enkeltfag from GSK used for programme subject levels. Confirm the individual route with AU. The rule is national rather than this university's: the Danish Agency for Higher Education and Science sets which examinations are adgangsgivende, and every Danish institution applies the same one. Two things about it are easy to get wrong. GSK (gymnasial supplering) cannot be used for this — GSK raises a subject level for someone who already holds a qualifying examination, so it meets a specific subject requirement but never raises the level of the examination itself. And the average used in quota 1 is the one from the first qualifying examination, so a Course Results holder who supplements or retakes is still converted on the original Course Results result.

Course Results under 18 points, or containing any subject at grade 1 or 2, are not a qualifying examination at all. A full IB Diploma of 24 points or more gives access to every higher education programme in Denmark.

requirements.label: A qualifying upper-secondary examination

officialWording.text: International Baccalaureate (IB) med IB-Course Result på mindst 18 point sidestilles med en gymnasial eksamen, hvis ansøgeren har opnået mindst karakteren 3 i hvert af de 6 fag, der indgår i IB-forløbet. Endvidere skal ansøgeren have gennemført enkeltfag på gymnasialt niveau svarende til overbygning, jf. reglerne om overbygning i højere forberedelseseksamen (hf-eksamen) i lov om gymnasiale uddannelser.

requirements.alternativeRoute: It does not close this one to you. The Danish Agency treats DP Course Results of at least 18 points, with at least grade 3 in all six subjects and at least three of them at HL, as equivalent to a qualifying examination for a Danish university bachelor once you have added two successive raises in the level of upper-secondary subjects, at least one of them to A level, taken as hf-enkeltfag or as a self-study candidate. If you already hold an A-level subject other than Danish, two raises to B level are enough. Retaking to be awarded the full IB Diploma is the other published route.
requirements.note: AU’s Course Results page still mentions GSK, but national guidance distinguishes qualification supplementation through HF-enkeltfag from GSK used for programme subject levels. Confirm the individual route with AU. The rule is national rather than this university's: the Danish Agency for Higher Education and Science sets which examinations are adgangsgivende, and every Danish institution applies the same one. Two things about it are easy to get wrong. GSK (gymnasial supplering) cannot be used for this — GSK raises a subject level for someone who already holds a qualifying examination, so it meets a specific subject requirement but never raises the level of the examination itself. And the average used in quota 1 is the one from the first qualifying examination, so a Course Results holder who supplements or retakes is still converted on the original Course Results result.

officialWording.text: International Baccalaureate (IB) med IB-Course Result på mindst 18 point sidestilles med en gymnasial eksamen, hvis ansøgeren har opnået mindst karakteren 3 i hvert af de 6 fag, der indgår i IB-forløbet. requirements.alternativeRoute: It does not close this one to you. The Danish Agency treats DP Course Results of at least 18 points, with at least grade 3 in all six subjects and at least three of them at HL, as equivalent to a qualifying examination for a Danish university bachelor once you have added two successive raises in the level of upper-secondary subjects, at least one of them to A level, taken as hf-enkeltfag or as a self-study candidate. If you already hold an A-level subject other than Danish, two raises to B level are enough. Retaking to be awarded the full IB Diploma is the other published route.
requirements.note: AU’s Course Results page still mentions GSK, but national guidance distinguishes qualification supplementation through HF-enkeltfag from GSK used for programme subject levels. Confirm the individual route with AU. The rule is national rather than this university's: the Danish Agency for Higher Education and Science sets which examinations are adgangsgivende, and every Danish institution applies the same one. Two things about it are easy to get wrong. GSK (gymnasial supplering) cannot be used for this — GSK raises a subject level for someone who already holds a qualifying examination, so it meets a specific subject requirement but never raises the level of the examination itself. And the average used in quota 1 is the one from the first qualifying examination, so a Course Results holder who supplements or retakes is still converted on the original Course Results result.

DP Course Results (formerly the IB Certificate) of at least 18 points, with at least grade 3 in all six subjects and at least three subjects at HL, are a qualifying examination in Denmark on the same terms as a two-year hf without overbygning: they give access to erhvervsakademi- and professionsbachelor programmes through quota 1 and quota 2, and to a university bachelor only after two successive raises of upper-secondary subject level, at least one to A level, taken as hf-enkeltfag. Course Results under 18 points, or containing any subject at grade 1 or 2, are not a qualifying examination at all. A full IB Diploma of 24 points or more gives access to every higher education programme in Denmark.
sources.quote: IB-elever uden IB Diploma, men med mindst 18 point (Diploma Programme (DP) Course Results), har adgang til videregående uddannelser i Danmark på lige vilkår med ansøgere med den 2-årige hf-eksamen uden overbygning. Det kræver, at alle 6 IB-fag (3 HL-fag og 3 SL- eller 4 HL-fag og 2 SL-fag) er bestået med mindst karakteren 3. Det betyder, at de har adgang til at søge optagelse på erhvervsakademi- og professionsbacheloruddannelser gennem kvote 1 og 2. Ansøgere med et Diploma Programme (DP) Course Results på mindst 18 point og mindst karakteren 3 i alle fag kan derudover få adgang til en universitetsbacheloruddannelse gennem kvote 1 og 2 ved enten at supplere med enkeltfag efter samme regler som hf’erne eller tage deres IB-eksamen om for at få et IB Diploma – Retake.
